title: Set 86

sentences.ko: 다른 지점 자리를 제안받았어요. 연봉이 6천 달러쯤 더 많고요. 대신 편도 40분을 운전해야 해요. 자꾸 하자고 저를 설득하게 돼요. 조건만 놓고 보면 당연히 하겠다고 해야 하니까요. 그러다 딸 재우는 시간에 집에 못 있는 걸 생각하면 다시 원점이에요. 이럴 땐 대체 어떻게 해야 돼요?
sentences.text: They offered me the spot at the other office and it's about six thousand dollars more, but I'd be driving forty minutes each way. And I keep talking myself into it, because on paper I should just say yes. Then I think about not being home for my daughter's bedtime and I'm right back where I started. What would you even do with that?

alts.text: So they want me at the other office, and it's like six thousand dollars more, but that's forty minutes in the car each way. And I keep telling myself just do it, because on paper it's a yes. Then I picture missing my daughter's bedtime and I'm right back where I started. What would you even do?

They have offered me the position at the other office, and it is approximately six thousand dollars more, but it would mean driving forty minutes in each direction. I keep persuading myself to accept, because on paper I should simply agree. Then I consider not being home for my daughter's bedtime, and I am back where I began. What would you do in that situation?

sentences.note: **talking myself into it** 은 내키지 않는 일을 스스로 설득해서 하기로 만드는 겁니다. **on paper** 는 조건만 놓고 보면, 서류상으로는 이라는 뜻이고, **right back where I started** 는 다시 제자리로 돌아왔다는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 친구한테 고민 상담하면서 결론은 못 내리기

sentences.ko: 집에 들어가서 코트도 채 못 벗었는데 이모가 시작하세요. 만나는 사람은 있냐, 아직 그 회사 다니냐, 애는 언제 낳을 거냐. 그걸 다 대답해요. 달리 어쩌겠어요, 일흔이신데. 그러더니 삼촌이 방 안 사람들 다 들리게 저더러 피곤해 보인다고 하시고요. 그래서 빨리 먹고 여덟 시에는 그 집에서 나왔어요.
sentences.text: I walk in and my aunt starts before I've got my coat off, am I seeing anybody, am I still at the same job, when are we having kids. And I'm answering all of it, because what else are you going to do, she's seventy. Then my uncle announces to the whole room that I look tired. So I ate fast and I was out of there by eight.

alts.text: So I get there and my aunt's on me before my coat's even off, am I seeing anybody, am I still at the same job, when are we having kids. And I answer all of it, cause what are you gonna do, she's seventy. Then my uncle tells the whole room I look tired. So I ate fast and I was gone by eight.

I arrived, and my aunt began before I had even removed my coat, asking whether I was seeing anyone, whether I was still at the same job, and when we intended to have children. I answered all of it, because there was little else I could do, she is seventy. Then my uncle announced to the entire room that I looked tired. I ate quickly and left by eight.

sentences.note: **before I've got my coat off** 는 코트도 벗기 전에, 그러니까 들어서자마자라는 뜻입니다. **what else are you going to do** 는 달리 어쩌겠냐고 체념할 때 쓰고, **out of there by eight** 은 여덟 시에는 이미 그 자리를 떴다는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 친척들 모인 자리에서 질문 공세 받은 얘기

sentences.ko: 이번 주말에 두 가지를 거절했는데 또 그러라고 해도 그럴 거예요. 토요일에는 네 시까지 옷도 안 갈아입고 있었고, 제대로 끝낸 거라고는 3월부터 붙잡고 있던 책 한 권뿐이에요. 아내는 무슨 일 있냐고 계속 물어봤어요. 평소에는 제가 한 시간도 가만히 못 앉아 있으니까요. 그런데 월요일에 진짜 푹 쉰 상태로 출근했어요. 그런 일은 정말 없거든요.
sentences.text: I said no to two different things this weekend and I'd do it again. I was in the same clothes until four on Saturday, and the only thing I actually finished was a book I've had since March. My wife kept asking if something was wrong, because normally I can't sit still for an hour. But I went in Monday actually rested, and that basically never happens.

alts.text: Turned down two things this weekend and no regrets. Was in the same clothes till four on Saturday, and the only thing I actually got through was a book I've had since March. My wife kept asking if something was up, cause normally I can't sit still for an hour. But I got in Monday actually rested, and that pretty much never happens.

I declined two separate things this weekend, and I would do so again. I remained in the same clothes until four on Saturday, and the only thing I actually finished was a book I have had since March. My wife kept asking whether something was wrong, because ordinarily I cannot sit still for an hour. However, I arrived on Monday genuinely rested, and that essentially never happens.

sentences.note: **said no to** 는 거절했다는 뜻입니다. **I can't sit still** 은 가만히 앉아 있지를 못한다, 뭐라도 해야 직성이 풀린다는 말이고, **that basically never happens** 는 그런 일은 거의 없다고 덧붙일 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: 주말에 아무것도 안 하고 쉰 게 좋았다고 말하기

sentences.ko: 토요일에 동생 지하실에 바닥 까는 걸 도왔는데, 저는 그런 걸 살면서 해 본 적이 없어요. 알고 보니 동생도 마찬가지였고요. 네 시간쯤 지났을 때 둘이 서서 폰으로 영상 보면서 어디서 잘못됐는지 찾고 있었어요. 지금은 괜찮아요, 대체로는. 계단 옆 모서리만 안 보시면 돼요.
sentences.text: So I helped my brother put a floor in his basement on Saturday, and I've never done that in my life, and it turns out neither has he. Four hours in we're standing there watching a video on his phone trying to figure out where we went wrong. It's fine now, mostly. Just don't look at the corner by the stairs.

alts.text: So my brother and I put a floor in his basement Saturday, and I've never done that in my life, and turns out he hasn't either. Four hours in we're just standing there watching a video on his phone trying to work out where we went wrong. It's fine now, mostly. Just don't look at the corner by the stairs.

On Saturday I helped my brother install a floor in his basement, and I have never done that in my life, and as it turns out, neither has he. Four hours in, we were standing there watching a video on his phone, trying to determine where we had gone wrong. It is fine now, for the most part. Simply do not look at the corner by the stairs.

sentences.note: **it turns out** 은 알고 보니라는 뜻이고, 뒤이은 **neither has he** 는 그 사람도 해 본 적 없다고 받는 말입니다. **Four hours in** 은 시작하고 네 시간쯤 됐을 때를 가리킵니다.

sentences.ko: 같은 층에 근무하는 사람이 있는데, 상상할 수 있는 가장 사소한 메일에까지 제 상사를 참조로 넣어요. 파일 보냈냐고 묻는 정도의 메일에요. 그러고는 2분 뒤에 걸어와서 저한테 직접 물어봐요. 그러니까 급한 것도 아니잖아요. 그래서 저는 이제 한 줄로만 답하고 말아요. 아내는 그냥 신경 쓰인다고 말하라는데, 아마 맞는 말이겠죠. 그런데 막상 입으로 말해 보면 별일도 아닌 것처럼 들려요.
sentences.text: There's a guy on my floor who copies my manager on the most basic email you can imagine, like asking if I've sent a file yet. And then he'll walk over two minutes later and just ask me himself, so it's not like he's in a hurry. I've started answering him in one line and nothing else. My wife says just tell him it bothers me, and she's probably right, but it sounds like nothing when you say it out loud.

alts.text: We've got a guy on my floor who copies my manager on the most basic email you can think of, like did I send that file yet. And then he'll come over two minutes later and just ask me himself, so it's not like he's in a rush. Now I just answer him in one line and that's it. My wife says just tell him it bugs me, and she's probably right, but it sounds like nothing when you say it out loud.

There is a colleague on my floor who copies my manager on the most trivial email imaginable, such as asking whether I have sent a file yet. He will then walk over two minutes later and ask me himself, so it is not as though he is in any hurry. I have begun answering him in a single line and nothing else. My wife says I should simply tell him that it bothers me, and she is probably right, but it sounds like nothing when said aloud.

sentences.note: **copies my manager on** 은 메일에 상사를 참조로 넣는다는 뜻입니다. **it's not like he's in a hurry** 는 급한 것도 아니면서라고 꼬집는 말이고, **it sounds like nothing when you say it out loud** 은 입 밖에 내면 대수롭지 않게 들린다는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: 회사 사람 때문에 짜증난 걸 친구한테 털어놓기

reviewed: 1번 한국어의 "당신 같으면" 은 친구에게 하는 말로는 쓰지 않는 말투라 "이럴 땐 대체 어떻게 해야 돼요?" 로 고쳤습니다.
2번 formal 이 "I arrived" 로 시작해 놓고 뒤에서 "whether I am seeing anyone" 처럼 현재로 흘러 시제가 어긋났습니다. 격식체 간접화법에 맞게 과거로 맞췄습니다.
3번 casual 이 첫 동사만 바꾸고 나머지가 text 와 거의 같았습니다. 게다가 "turned down" 은 "said no to" 보다 오히려 더 격식에 가깝습니다. 주어를 떨어뜨린 구어체로 다시 썼습니다.
4번 casual 의 "my brother had me putting a floor in" 은 동생이 시켜서 했다는 뜻이 되어 원문(내가 도왔다)과 내용이 달라집니다. 뜻을 지키면서 첫머리는 겹치지 않게 "my brother and I put a floor in" 으로 고쳤습니다.
